definitions.hv21 / hv63 / hv252: Realized volatility, close to close: the sample standard deviation of the daily log returns of the last 21, 63 and 252 sessions, multiplied by the square root of 252, in percent a year. 16% a year is about 1% a day.
definitions.yz21: Yang-Zhang volatility over the last 21 sessions, annualized the same way: the variance of the overnight gap, plus the variance of the open-to-close move, plus the intraday range (Rogers-Satchell), weighted as Yang and Zhang (2000) weight them. It reads the whole bar, so a stock that gaps and reverses inside the day is not read as quiet.
definitions.atr: The chart's ATR %: the average true range of the last 14 sessions as a percent of the last close. The true range of a session is the largest of its high minus its low, its high minus the previous close, and the previous close minus its low.
definitions.hvp: Where today's 21-session volatility stands among the stock's own last 252 daily readings of it, 0 to 100: the share of those readings below it plus half the share equal to it. 95 means the stock has rarely been this volatile in a year; 5 that it has rarely been this quiet. Blank under 126 readings.
definitions.hv21p: The stock's 21-session volatility as it stood 21 sessions ago. Today's reading above it: volatility is rising; below it: falling. Change is today's reading minus that one, in points.
definitions.mx / mxd: The largest one-session close-to-close move of the last 63 sessions, with its sign, and the session it printed on.
definitions.sp_d / sp_w / sp_m / sp_q: Price spread: how far the highest high of the window stood above its lowest low, in percent - (high / low - 1) x 100. d is the last session's own bar, w the last 5 sessions, m the last 21, q the last 63.
definitions.hi / lo: The highest high and the lowest low of that window, in dollars, on bars rebased for splits.
definitions.pos: Where the last close sits inside the window's spread: 0 at the low, 100 at the high.
definitions.own: Where the window's spread stands among the stock's own last 252 windows of the same length (one ending on each session), 0 to 100. 95 means an unusually wide spread for this stock; 5 an unusually narrow one. Blank under 126 windows.
definitions.rk_*: Rank inside the row's own kind - stocks against stocks, ETFs against ETFs - 1 is the most volatile (21 and 63 sessions) or the widest spread (day, week, month, quarter). A measure that is set aside has no rank.
definitions.aside / why: A row that is set aside is measured but left out of every ranking, every board and the market's medians; why says which of four reasons applies - jump (a flagged jump inside the last 63 sessions), print (a flagged print inside them), thin, or pinned - and aside names the measures (all six). The figures still print.
definitions.pinned: A stock whose last 21 sessions fit inside 3.5% from the lowest low to the highest high. A freely trading company does not do that (the S&P 500 fund's own month is wider); a company whose takeover price is agreed does. Pinned names are listed on their own and kept out of the rankings and the market's medians.
definitions.jd / jr / ja: A flagged jump: the date, the ratio and the sessions since a one-session close-to-close move beyond 3-to-1 either way, inside the last 300 sessions, that no recorded or inferred split explains. It can be a real collapse or a corporate action the record does not carry.
definitions.pd / pr / pa: A flagged print: the date, the ratio and the sessions since a bar whose high stood more than 3 times above, or whose low more than 3 times below, every close around it - the close before, its own and the close after. No trade beside it supports that price, so it is read as one bad print rather than a range; ratio is that high or low over the nearest of those closes.
definitions.miss: How many of the last 63 sessions the symbol printed no bar on (sessions before its first bar are not counted). More than 3 and the row is thin: its windows cover more calendar days than they say, so it is set aside.
definitions.boards: Each board is the 25 names at one end of one measure, among common stocks worth $1B or more whose measure is not set aside. Rising / falling is the 21-session volatility minus its reading 21 sessions ago.
definitions.bands: Stocks counted by their 21-session volatility: under 15%, 15-25%, 25-40%, 40-60%, 60-100%, 100% and over - with the market value in each band.
definitions.universe: Listed common stocks (no OTC, preferreds, warrants, units, rights, shells) and ETFs that are not geared or inverse, with a 20-session average dollar volume of at least the floor, a bar in the last 3 sessions and at least 22 sessions of their own continuous history. A line the factor book calls common stock is still left out when its own name says it is a note or a preferred share, or when it is a second NASDAQ issue of a listed company (fifth letter G-J, L-P, Z or W, the issuer's name, under a tenth of the dollar volume of the ticker it extends).

limitations: This is realized volatility: what the closes and bars already printed. It is not implied volatility - no option is read - and it is not a forecast.
The windows are sessions, not calendar periods: a week is the last 5 sessions, a month 21, a quarter 63.

Pinned is read from the tape alone (21 sessions inside 3.5%); no deal record is consulted. A deal agreed inside the last month still shows as a jump in its windows, and a cash-and-stock deal can keep floating.
Bars are rebased for splits here (recorded, then inferred) but not for dividends. A large special dividend prints as a move.

A split inferred from the tape alone is accepted only when the session opened at the new price (the gap from the prior close carries at least half of the move). A fall that happened inside the session is kept as a fall, and flagged as a jump when it is beyond 3-to-1.

A collapse is a wide spread: a stock that fell 99% in the quarter prints a spread near 10,000%, because the spread is the high over the low. Reverse splits are rebased, so such a fall is the holder's own.
The bank begins 2021-08-26; a listing younger than a window leaves that window blank.
